intro: If you're looking for a place to stay in Ban Chang with "condo-sized rooms," a kitchen you can actually cook in, a balcony to relax on, and a pool for an evening dip — Grand Garden Hotel & Residence is the name many locals think of first · It's not a luxury beachfront resort, but an aparthotel in central Ban Chang that positions itself as a "second home" for workers around Map Ta Phut and U-Tapao, as well as families who want more space than a typical hotel room at an easy price · Open since 2002, every room has a kitchenette and a balcony, starting at about THB 1,200/night, and it's only a few minutes' drive from Nam Rin Beach and Pala Beach · TripAdvisor ranks it #2 of 11 hotels in Ban Chang

body.html: Overview — who Grand Garden Hotel & Residence suits · The fastest way to understand this place is that it's an "aparthotel" more than a purely tourist hotel · The main draw is residence-style rooms that are far bigger than a typical hotel room, with a kitchenette, fridge, microwave and a lounge sofa all in the same unit, which suits people staying several nights or who'd rather cook than eat out every meal · Open since 2002, it sits in central Ban Chang, Ban Chang District, Rayong Province — a district between the Map Ta Phut industrial estate and U-Tapao Airport, so it's no surprise that most regulars are local workers, both Thai and foreign, on medium- to long-term projects · From real reviews across several platforms, the picture is consistent: the people this place suits are workers on long stays, families who want a lot of space on a budget, and travellers who need somewhere near U-Tapao or Map Ta Phut at an accessible price rather than tourists chasing a beachfront resort vibe · To put it plainly, if you're picturing falling asleep to the sound of waves and walking straight from your room onto the sand, this isn't the answer — but if you want a roomy, convenient base with a kitchen and a pool, within a short drive of both the beach and work, it does that job well for the price

Location and getting around · Grand Garden Hotel & Residence sits on Pala Beach Road in Ban Chang's municipal area, which counts as the "town centre" of Ban Chang, with convenience stores, local restaurants, a market and various shops close by · What makes this location valuable in the eyes of workers is that it's right in the middle of everything — about 10–15 min drive from U-Tapao Airport (UTP), about 10–15 min from the Map Ta Phut industrial estate, and about 30 min into Rayong town, with Pattaya about 40 min away · As for the coast, Nam Rin Beach and Pala Beach — Ban Chang's quiet beaches — are a short few-minute drive away, so even though the hotel isn't beachfront, you can still go chill by the sea in the evening · One thing worth knowing is that Ban Chang has little public transport, so having your own car or a rental makes things much easier; without a car you'll rely on hired vehicles or ride-hailing apps, which can be hard to find at certain times · If you fly into U-Tapao and want somewhere near the airport to rest before moving on, this location has a real edge on travel time

"The room was huge, like having a whole condo — a kitchenette, fridge and microwave, the lot. We stayed several nights for work so we could cook our own meals, way cheaper than eating out every time. The staff were really helpful too."

Room types and decor · Grand Garden's strength is mainly its "room size" · Almost every room type is a residence-style unit larger than a standard 3-star hotel room, and comes with a kitchenette, microwave, fridge, sofa and private balcony · From the available room information, options range from a Superior Double with balcony as the entry room, to a larger Grand Deluxe (twin/king), up to a One Bedroom Suite and a large Studio for families or long-stayers who want a work area in the room · The decor is simple and practical, focused on function over flash — wooden furniture, warm tones, a work desk, flat-screen TV, safe and air-conditioning in every room · Many real reviews agree that the rooms are spacious, clean, well-equipped and good for long stays, and anyone tired of cramped hotel rooms will feel they can "breathe" here · But to be straight about it, some voices note that the building and parts of the furnishings are starting to show their age (open since 2002), some beds are fairly firm, and details like doors or finishing aren't as tidy as in a new hotel · Overall these are rooms that are "good value and genuinely usable" rather than flawlessly pretty, and people who set their expectations on space and function tend to come away satisfied

Facilities and the pool · Even as a mid-sized hotel in a small town, Grand Garden has facilities that are complete enough for a long stay · The highlight many people mention is the outdoor pool set in the green garden around the hotel, perfect for a cooling dip in the evening after work or a day at the beach · There's also a gym for those who want to work out during their stay, an in-house restaurant, a 24-hour reception, an airport shuttle (ask in advance), free Wi-Fi throughout, and free parking, which matters a lot in a town where everyone has to drive · What sets this place apart from a typical hotel is having an "in-room kitchen" plus these shared facilities, which means it supports real long-term living, not just an overnight stay · One thing noted in reviews is that the building has no lift, so if you get an upper-floor room with heavy luggage you may have to take the stairs (staff usually help carry), and the pool is a medium-sized one for soaking and relaxing rather than a long lap pool for serious swimming · Overall, at this price it gives you quite a bit more than you'd expect

Food and dining · The hotel has its own restaurant and serves a buffet breakfast that several reviews call "decent and filling" to start the day, with basic Thai and international dishes · An interesting point is that some reviews mention a Japanese restaurant on the hotel grounds with fresh ingredients and good flavour, which you don't often find at a place of this level in a small town like Ban Chang · But the real heart of eating at Grand Garden is the "in-room kitchen" — because every room has a kitchenette, fridge and microwave, many long-stay guests choose to buy from convenience stores or markets in Ban Chang and cook in their room, which saves a lot compared with eating out every meal · Around the hotel there are plenty of local restaurants and Ban Chang seafood spots to choose from, at friendly prices · The takeaway on food is that this place doesn't stand out for a fancy in-house dining room, but for the "flexibility" to choose between a buffet breakfast, cooking for yourself, or going out to try restaurants in town — which fits the long-stay style nicely

Service and staff · Service is a point that earns fairly consistent praise in real reviews · Many guests say the reception staff and housekeepers are friendly, helpful and attentive, especially with the little things like carrying bags up to the room when there's no lift, recommending restaurants in town, or helping with transport · For long-stay guests, getting to know the staff makes it feel like staying somewhere that's looked after · That said, to be fair, some voices in reviews note that some staff speak limited English, which can be a minor hurdle for foreign guests who don't speak Thai, and there are occasional reports of rooms not being ready at the stated check-in time · These notes are common at local accommodation in general, and most can be handled by communicating ahead and allowing extra time · Overall the team's kindness remains a strength that brings many guests back

Voices from real reviews (the good and the bad) · Pulling together TripAdvisor, Hotels.com, Expedia and other booking platforms, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: rooms are very spacious, like getting a whole condo; a complete kitchen and equipment, great for long stays; a lovely pool with a leafy garden setting; a filling, decent buffet breakfast; a good in-house Japanese restaurant; helpful, friendly staff; free parking and a location near U-Tapao and Map Ta Phut · On the watch-out side: the most talked-about issue is that the building and some of the upkeep are starting to feel old and worn with age — open since 2002, some beds are firm, doors don't close fully, or walls are fairly thin so you can hear the neighbouring room · Next are no lift, meaning stairs if you get an upper-floor room; some staff speak limited English; and some reviews warn there's an outdoor karaoke nearby that can be loud until around midnight on weekend nights · Another interesting point is price — some foreign reviews suggest the walk-in rate at the counter can sometimes be cheaper than the online platform price, so it's worth comparing several channels before deciding · These criticisms reflect that this is local accommodation that's "good value" rather than a flawless new hotel, and people who set their expectations accordingly tend to be happy with what they get

"The room was clean and the staff were lovely and helpful · My only gripe is that on weekend nights there was a bit of karaoke noise from outside that went on late. If you're a light sleeper, ask for an inner room, and note the building has no lift so you'll be walking up the stairs."

Price comparison and value · Room rates at Grand Garden Hotel & Residence are very accessible for what you get · An entry room like the Superior is around THB 1,200–1,500/night at normal rates, while bigger rooms like the Grand Deluxe and One Bedroom Suite run roughly THB 1,800–2,800/night depending on size and season · Importantly, there are often monthly rates for workers on long stays, which are far better value than paying by the day — ask the hotel directly · Set against getting a residence-sized room with a full kitchen, plus a pool, gym, breakfast and free parking, this price level is good value among Ban Chang's budget stays, especially measured per square metre of room you get · The thing to weigh up is that you're trading newness and a polished building for room size and price — if you prioritise usable space, a kitchen and budget, this place delivers high value · But if you'd pay more for a new beachfront room with a view, you may want to look at resorts on the Mae Ramphueng Beach side or other Rayong beaches instead

Things to know before booking · A few things help make the stay smoother · One, compare prices across several channels — both online platforms and asking the hotel directly, especially for long stays where you should ask about weekly or monthly rates · Two, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for an inner room that doesn't face the road, or one on the side away from the karaoke, because weekend nights can get loud late, and some walls are fairly thin · Three, since the building has no lift, if you have heavy luggage or are travelling with older people, ask for a ground-floor room when you book · Four, Ban Chang is easiest with your own car; without one, plan your trips to the beach or into town in advance · Five, if you mean to cook, the in-room kitchen has the basics, but check with the hotel how complete the kitchenware is for the dishes you want to make · Six, confirm the U-Tapao Airport shuttle in advance if you need it, because it's close but public transport is scarce

Verdict · From all the real reviews, Grand Garden Hotel & Residence is the best fit for workers around Map Ta Phut and U-Tapao, families who want a big room with a kitchen, and travellers who need a budget base near the airport and Ban Chang's beaches · Its strengths are spacious residence-sized rooms with a full kitchen, plus a pool, gym, breakfast, free parking and a helpful team — all at a price that's hard to find elsewhere · If you're planning a long stay or cooking for yourself, this place is very good value · But if you're after a brand-new, flawless hotel, a beachfront room with a view, or a pure holiday-resort vibe, this may not be the right choice, since it's an older building in the town centre rather than by the beach · In short, Grand Garden is Ban Chang's "genuinely usable second home" more than a holiday hotel — and in that role, it's done well enough to rank near the top of town for years

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Grand Garden Hotel & Residence Ban Chang

faq.q: Where is Grand Garden Hotel & Residence · is it far to Nam Rin Beach?
faq.a: The hotel is in central Ban Chang, on Pala Beach Road, Ban Chang District, Rayong Province · It's about a 5–10 min drive from Nam Rin Beach and about 10 min from Pala Beach · It's near U-Tapao Airport and the Map Ta Phut estate at about 10–15 min, about 30 min into Rayong town, and about 40 min to Pattaya · Since public transport is scarce, having your own car is easiest

faq.q: Do Grand Garden's rooms really have a kitchen · are they good for long stays?
faq.a: Yes · the standout here is that every room is residence-style with a kitchenette, fridge, microwave, sofa and balcony, and the rooms are bigger than a typical hotel · They're great for local workers and families on long stays, because you can cook your own meals, and monthly rates are often available — just ask

faq.q: What's the starting price at Grand Garden Hotel · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 1,200/night for a Superior room with balcony at normal rates · There are Grand Deluxe, Studio and One Bedroom Suite options for families or long stays, at around THB 1,600–2,600 · Some reviews note the walk-in rate can be cheaper than online at certain times, so compare several channels before booking

faq.q: Who is Grand Garden Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for workers around Map Ta Phut and U-Tapao, families who want a big room with a kitchen, and travellers who need a budget base near the airport and Ban Chang's beaches · If you're after a beachfront resort vibe or a brand-new hotel, resorts on the Mae Ramphueng Beach side or Koh Samet may suit you better

faq.q: What are the noise and building condition like at Grand Garden?
faq.a: It's a building that's been open since 2002, so it has signs of age and no lift · Some rooms have firm beds and fairly thin walls, and weekend nights may have karaoke noise nearby until late · If you're a light sleeper, we suggest asking for an inner room away from the road, and if you have heavy luggage, ask for a ground-floor room when you book

faq.q: Does Grand Garden Hotel have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes · there's an outdoor pool in a leafy garden and a gym · It serves a buffet breakfast that reviews call filling and decent, and there's an in-house Japanese restaurant praised for its freshness · There's also free Wi-Fi, free parking and a 24-hour reception
